body.p: In response to the Office Action dated June 21, 2024, claims 1, 11, 13, and 18-19 are amended, claim 12 is canceled, and claims 2-10, 14-17, and 20 remain unchanged.
Amendment made for claim 1 is supported by paragraph 0036 of the specification.
Amendment made for claim 11 is supported by original claim 12.
Amendment made for claim 18 is supported by paragraphs 0032, 0046-0047 and 0052 of the specification.
The other amendments are made for clarity.
Therefore, the amendment can be supported by original application.
Claims 1, 11, and 18 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over LIN in view of OURA.

Claims 2-10, 12-17, and 19-20 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
Amended claim 1 now recites:
"A method of managing monitoring data based on a probe assembly, comprising:
establishing, by the probe assembly, communication connection with a first monitor;

receiving, by the probe assembly in response to a data-transfer instruction, first monitoring data from the first monitor; after transferring the first monitoring data being completed, disconnecting the communication connection with the first monitor; wherein, the first monitoring data comprises: monitoring data collected by the probe assembly from a patient, emergency treatment information recorded by the first monitor, and information of the patient;
establishing, by the probe assembly, communication connection with a second monitor; and
sending, by the probe assembly, at least the first monitoring data to the second monitor and performing, by the probe assembly, a monitoring task cooperatively with the second monitor".
The Office Action has admitted that LIN is silent in teaching the receiving step of the claimed method, but mentions that OURA discloses the receiving step.

The applicant respectfully disagrees. In the amended claim 1, in response to the data- transfer instruction, it is the first monitoring data from the first monitor that is received by the probe assembly, and claim 1 further defines what kinds of information shall be interpreted as the first monitoring data herein. It is the "monitoring data collected by the probe assembly from a patient, emergency treatment information recorded by the first monitor, and information of the patient" that can be interpreted as the first monitoring data, i.e., received by the probe assembly.
By contrast, the office action mentions the following:
image quality, etc), first monitoring data from the first monitor (0041 and 0059 teaches

Therefore, the office action analogizes the control signal, which is for instructing a change of setting to the probe head, to be a kind of first monitoring data. However, the specification of OURA does not describe in detail how the control signal is generated, but considering the function of the control signal (change in settings), it can be deducted that the control signal might be generated due to operations performed by medical care/nursing staff. At least, the control signal, which is for instructing a change of setting to the probe head, cannot be equivalent to a monitoring data collected from a patient; or any medical treatment; or any information of the patient.

In addition, the applicant believes that the terminology "monitoring" data itself already indicates that such data shall be obtained/generated from certain monitoring. However, the control signal for instructing a change of settings cannot be equivalent to any monitoring. Even if the "control signal" in OURA had any special technical meanings, the specification of OURA does not disclose that the "control signal" can be equivalent to any monitoring data.
Furthermore, in the sending operation of the method, amended claim 1 defines that it is the first monitoring data (mentioned in the receiving operation) that is sent to the second monitor.

The office action has admitted that LIN is silent in teaching the receiving step of the claimed method, and therefore, the data sent from the probe assembly to the second monitor in LIN shall not be equivalent to the first monitoring data of the present application.

If combining with the disclosure in OURA, OURA discloses that, in paragraph 0078, "The image capturing unit 12 may be configured to transmit a control signal to the probe head 11 via the patient monitor 20. The image capturing unit 12 transmits a control signal according to operation on the input interfaces (the input buttons 123 etc.) on the image capturing unit 12 to the patient monitor 20 by wired communication or by wireless communication. The patient monitor 20 detects whether the control signal is addressed to the patient monitor 20 or addressed to the probe head 11". Therefore, the control signal is not directly sent to the probe, instead, the control signal is sent to the monitor and is then sent to the probe (through the monitor).

The above disclosure means that, after the probe receives the data (control signal), the probe does not further send the data to another monitor. Instead, the probe is the termination of the data (control signal). Therefore, the data transfer (control signal transfer) in OURA in combination with LIN is different from the data transfer through the probe assembly as defined in claim 1 of the present application.
Therefore, regardless of whether the control signal in OURA being equivalent or

inequivalent to the monitoring data as defined in claim 1 of the present application, the data (control signal) in OURA and LIN cannot be transferred from one monitor to a probe and then to another monitor.

Therefore, amended claim 1 is novel and inventive over the prior art, and therefore, claim 1 is believed to be allowable. Claims 2-10 depend on and further limit claim 1, and therefore, claims 2-10 are also believed to be allowable.

All features in claim 12 are combined into claim 11. Therefore, claim 11 is claim 12 rewritten in the independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Therefore, claims 11 and 13-17 are believed to be allowable.
Amended claim 18 now recites that, in part:
"the probe assembly comprises at least one probe;

during receiving the first monitoring data from the first monitor, one probe of the at least one probe is selected to serve as a temporary host probe to receive and store the first monitoring data; and
the communication connection between the probe assembly and the first monitor is disconnected after transmitting the first monitoring data is completed".

As explained in claim 1, the probe assembly in the present application serves as a "transfer node" between two monitors, the same data is originated from the first monitor, transferred to the probe assembly, and is then transferred to the second monitor. When the data reaches the probe assembly, the probe assembly acts as a temporary host, and eventually, the data needs to be transferred to the second monitor.
However, none of the cited documents discloses such a "data transfer path" from the first monitor to the temporary host (probe) and further to the second monitor.

Therefore, amended claim 18 is novel and involves the inventive step over the prior art, and is believed to be allowable. Claims 19-20 depend on and further limit claim 18, and therefore, they are also believed to be allowable.
Applicant believes this reply is fully responsive to all outstanding issues and places this application in condition for allowance.
If anything remains which can be resolved on the telephone, the Examiner is invited to call the representative.
Respectfully submitted, /Leong C. Lei, #50402/
